text.tspan: Amazon MQ: managed ActiveMQ / RabbitMQ broker for open protocols (added: not in your notes)
SQS and SNS are cloud-native, proprietary AWS APIs. Apps from on-premises often use open protocols: MQTT, AMQP, STOMP, OpenWire, WSS (+ JMS APIs).
Migrating them? Instead of re-engineering to SQS/SNS, use Amazon MQ: change the endpoint, keep the messaging code.
• Has QUEUE features (~SQS) and TOPIC features (~SNS) in one broker.
• Runs on broker instances (e.g. mq.m5.large): pay per instance hour + storage; it does NOT scale like SQS/SNS (scale = bigger instance or network of brokers).
• Multi-AZ with failover: active/standby; the standby takes over the shared EFS storage if the active broker or its AZ fails.
• Keyword: "migrate an on-prem app that uses MQTT / AMQP / STOMP / JMS without code changes" → Amazon MQ. "New cloud app" → SQS/SNS.
